chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
"But whoever is pardoned anything by his brother, then follow-up should be according to what is right, and payment to him should be with excellence."

What is that thing? He said: "It is when a man accepts the blood money. So the man who has the right was commanded to pursue it in a fair manner and not to make things difficult for him, and the one upon whom the right is due was commanded to pay it to him with excellence when he is able."
I said: What do you say about His saying, the Exalted: "Then whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment"?
He said: "It is the man who accepts the blood money or makes a settlement, then afterwards commits an offense by mutilating or killing; so Allah has promised him a painful punishment."

key_terms.اعْتَدَى: transgressed by going beyond the permitted legal limit
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money accepted as compensation in place of retaliation
key_terms.بِإِحْسَانٍ: with excellence and good conduct in fulfilling payment
key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: in a fair and proper manner recognized as just
key_terms.عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ: a painful punishment promised for unlawful excess after settlement
key_terms.عُفِيَ: pardoned or remitted in the context of waiving direct retaliation

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about accepting diyah and not transgressing afterward mean in Shiʿi hadith?
ai.summary: This narration explains the Qur'anic ruling concerning pardon in cases involving retaliation, interpreting it as the acceptance of blood money or settlement. It emphasizes just conduct on both sides: the claimant must not be harsh in demanding payment, and the liable party must pay properly when able. It also warns that after accepting compensation, further retaliation is a grave transgression deserving painful punishment.
